title: The 15 -ilities every cloud architect must know
oneliner: Architecture quality is a checklist: availability, scalability, usability, adaptability, reliability, security, maintainability, sustainability, visibility, interoperability, extensibility, recoverability, resilience, performance, and cloudability.
says: He reads out the full list of fifteen -ilities and frames them as the baseline vocabulary of a cloud architect - the qualities you are expected to design for on purpose, not discover after go-live.
explained: This is his very first reel, and it sets the tone for the whole channel: architecture is a discipline of named, checkable qualities. Each -ility is a question you ask of a design. Availability asks what happens when something fails at 2 AM. Scalability asks what happens when traffic triples. Maintainability asks whether the next engineer can change the system without fear. Recoverability asks how fast you come back from disaster.

The practical use of the list is review discipline. Before calling a design done, walk the fifteen words and write one sentence for each: how does this system achieve it, and how would we know? The ones you cannot answer are your design risks. Architects are paid to make these qualities explicit and traded off consciously - you rarely maximize all fifteen, so choosing which matter most for this workload is the actual job.
takeaway: Save the list. Run every design review against all fifteen -ilities and write down how the system achieves each one; a blank answer is a design risk.
